Subject: Re: Observed packet drops on private link after Friday deploy

Markus / Redwood team,

We started seeing intermittent HTTP 502s and retransmits across the private link after your Friday config change. Flows that cross the Acme private edge are showing lots of fragments and occasional reassembly failures. We captured a set of flows and attached a pcap subset (acme-egress-pcap.tar.gz).

Initial notes from our side:
- DSCP values are being rewritten at our edge (we see DF set + small fragments).
- MSS observed on TCP handshake from your clients is ~1460, but subsequent segments show fragmentation.
- Some fragments are dropped on the on-prem firewall (stateful SG).

Can your team confirm whether any egress rewriting or path MTU changes were applied on your managed appliance during the Friday rollout? We're treating this as impacting a small but growing percentage of traffic to our telemetry endpoints.

Alex
Alex Rivera
NetOps Lead, Acme Telecom

Date: Fri, 19 Feb 2027 13:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Observed packet drops on private link after Friday deploy

Thanks Alex — I dug into the pcap. Key observations:
- We can reproduce the pattern: SYN/SYN-ACK MSS advertised 1460, then downstream segments show fragments with DF set cleared on the second hop.
- Fragment offsets suggest an MTU mismatch between our egress appliance (MTU 1500) and Acme's transit device which appears to be lowering effective MTU to ~1400 for certain marked flows.
- Critically, there's evidence of DSCP rewrite happening on Acme's edge which coincides with the start of fragmentation. When DSCP is rewritten, packets seem to get routed through a different edge path with a 1400 MTU limit.

Hypotheses:
1) DSCP rewrite triggers alternate path with lower MTU and stateful firewall on that path doesn't accept fragments.
2) Our egress node is not clamping MSS for outbound TCP sessions, so large segments are generated and then fragmented on the path.
3) NAT behavior: if an intermediate NAT is stripping DF or rewriting IP headers weirdly, reassembly fails at the firewall.

Immediate mitigations to propose:
- Configure MSS clamping on our egress (tcp_mss = 1360) to avoid fragmentation until path MTU is resolved.
- Request Acme to disable DSCP rewrite for Redwood flows or validate MTU on the alternate path.
- Temporarily allow fragmented packets (ICMP type/code checks) in the firewall SGs for the affected subnet while we debug.

I've attached a quick trace output (egress-trace-output.txt) with the packet offsets. Dev — can you stage the MSS clamp on the edge host in non-prod first and we can roll it to prod during a short window? Jonas, please flag if this needs a canary.

Irene
Irene Choi
Network Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Observed packet drops on private link after Friday deploy

I validated Irene's findings in our staging egress host. Summary of actions I can perform quickly:
- Stage MSS clamp via iptables mangle rule + tcpoption MSS (set to 1360) on the egress interface. Validation steps: run tcpdump and ensure no fragments for sample flows.
- Add temporary iptables rule to ACCEPT fragments for Redwood->Acme subnet (will be scoped and timeboxed).
- Schedule a 30-minute maintenance window tomorrow 02/23 02:00-02:30 UTC to roll the changes to prod (MSS clamp + SG relax).

Risk notes: the SG relax will increase exposure to fragmented packets; we'll restrict to Acme IP ranges and revoke rules after. MSS clamp is low risk but could alter path behavior for some legacy clients — will monitor closely.

I'll prepare a short runbook and a draft message for Acme with the proposed window. Markus / Marissa — please confirm the window or suggest alternate times.

—Dev
